text:
Ellie (People Ops): Quick one  Ravi's train got delayed overnight and he bought meals and one extra hotel night. He submitted a per-diem claim but used actual receipts for meals. Are we OK with actuals + extra night?

Ravi (Sales): Correct. Train diverted, had to stay in town overnight. Bought 3 meals (breakfast/lunch/dinner) and a single room at a nearby hotel. Paid with personal card because I couldn't reach company card.

Marco (Finance): Policy summary: for travel delays caused by carrier/incidents, we reimburse reasonable actual costs for lodging and meals if the traveler uses receipts. Typical per-diem applies for planned travel; interruptions due to delays are exceptions. Need manager approval and documentation.

Ellie (People Ops): What docs do we want? I assume receipts + proof of delay (rail operator incident email or screenshot) + manager sign-off?

Marco (Finance): Exactly. Upload: 1) itemized hotel folio or receipt, 2) meal receipts (credit card or merchant), 3) train operator disruption notice (screenshot or email), and 4) manager approval line in expense comments or an approval email.

Lena (Manager): I approved Ravi's extra night and meals at the time via Slack. Do we need a formal email?

Ellie (People Ops): Verbal/Slack ok if it's clearly from the manager and timestamped, but Finance prefers an explicit approval string in the expense system or a short follow-up email for auditability. Can you paste your Slack approval into the expense comment?

Lena (Manager): Done  I added: "Approved extra night for Ravi due to OOS train delay on 03/15. Manager: Lena."

Ravi (Sales): One more nuance: meals are in local currency and some receipts are small cash tips without merchants on them. Do we accept cash meal receipts?

Marco (Finance): Accept cash receipts if they are legible and show merchant/date/amount. If missing merchant, add a short attestation in the expense describing the item and why no merchant print exists. For tips, include them on the same receipt where possible.

Ellie (People Ops): Any thresholds? If meals per day exceed a certain amount, do we need People Ops review versus manager-only?

Marco (Finance): Meals under $75/day per traveler are manager-approvable in incident cases. If total incidental extras > $200 (hotel/night + meals combined), escalate to People Ops for review. This one looks under that but we'll confirm once receipts uploaded.

travel-bot: Policy excerpt: "Unplanned lodging and meal costs due to transportation interruptions are reimbursable with receipts and manager approval. For foreign currency, attach currency conversion (XE or bank rate) or use card statement. See internal travel policy page." :link:

Ravi (Sales): Thanks, uploading receipts now and adding train operator notice + Lena's approval.

Ellie (People Ops): Great. Marco will process once attachments and coding are added. Closing when reimbursed.
